script: When I was fifteen, my heart would race before every class. For years I thought something was broken in me. What helped me see it differently: anxiety isn't a glitch, it's an alarm doing its job, just a little too loud. I wrote the book I wish I'd had back then.
broll_prompt: Multi-shot cinematic vertical sequence, handheld 24fps with subtle micro-jitter, practical lighting, film grain. SHOT 1 (0-2s): extreme close-up of a trembling teenage hand gripping a cold metal classroom doorknob, shallow depth of field, anxious tension. SHOT 2 (2-5s): fast POV glimpses, a cluttered school desk, a phone screen lighting up, shallow nervous breaths fogging a cold window, dim blue tones. SHOT 3 (5-9s): the camera slowly pulls back as warm amber morning light floods into the dark room, a volume dial slowly turning down, tension releasing, transition from cold blue to warm light. SHOT 4 (9-15s): a steady hand now writing calmly in an open notebook, pen pressure on paper, a slow page turn, a quiet exhale, hopeful warm cinematic tone. No faces, no text overlays.
